knowledge_point.title: Identifying the Horizontal Shift of a Horizontally Stretched Tangent or Cotangent Curve

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186184149/plots/e5690a634385eeb22814479d-prompt.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3}+C),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2},$ what is the value of $C?$ The dashed curve is $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3}).$ The horizontal displacement between the two marked zeros is $\frac{9\pi }{7}$ units to the right.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parameter $C$ determines a horizontal shift of $-3C$ units, modulo the period $3\pi$.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3}+C) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{1}{3}(x+3C))\end{aligned}
$$

The factor $x+3C$ indicates that the graph of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{1}{3}(x+3C))$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3}).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186184149/plots/e5690a634385eeb22814479d-solution.png)

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{x}{3})$ by $\frac{9\pi }{7}$ units to the right. Therefore:

$$
3C=-\frac{9\pi }{7}\,⟹\,C=-\frac{3\pi }{7}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $-\frac{3\pi }{7}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $-\frac{3\pi }{7}.$

question.:question/problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186184149/plots/7a2604d9b49f89ad29b688ba-prompt.png)

The graph above shows the function $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{3x}{2}+C),$ where $C$ is a constant. Given that $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2},$ what is the value of $C?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The parameter $C$ determines a horizontal shift of $-\frac{2C}{3}$ units, modulo the period $\frac{2\pi }{3}$.

First, we rewrite the function by factoring the horizontal stretch factor, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{3x}{2}+C) \\  & =\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{3}{2}(x+\frac{2C}{3}))\end{aligned}
$$

The factor $x+\frac{2C}{3}$ indicates that the graph of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{3}{2}(x+\frac{2C}{3}))$ is a horizontal translation of $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{3x}{2}).$ Comparing the two graphs below allows us to determine the amount of this shift.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/scratch/17592186184149/plots/7a2604d9b49f89ad29b688ba-solution.png)

From the diagram, we see that our curve has been obtained by shifting $y=\operatorname{cot}⁡(\frac{3x}{2})$ by $\frac{\pi }{3}-\frac{\pi }{4}=\frac{\pi }{12}$ units to the left. Therefore:

$$
\frac{2C}{3}=\frac{\pi }{12}\,⟹\,C=(\frac{\pi }{12})(\frac{3}{2})\,⟹\,C=\frac{\pi }{8}
$$

Since $-\frac{\pi }{2}<C<\frac{\pi }{2}$ and $\frac{\pi }{8}$ is in this interval, the value of $C$ is $\frac{\pi }{8}.$
